  Regular Meeting of March 10, 2021

Call to Order

Roll Call:  The March 10, 2021 meeting of the Transportation Commission
was held Via Zoom

Present:  Steven Placido, Henry Aviles, Cliff Bender, Antonio Chavira, Gwen
Chen, Lilian De Loza Gutierrez, Albert Lu, Kaysa Moreno, Kristopher Fortin

Absent:  Antonio Chavira

Also in attendance, Traffic Engineer Jana Robbins, Alhambra Police Department
Traffic Sergeant Castillo and Commission Secretary Martin Ray.

1. Traffic Safety Review of Main Street between Westmont Drive to Hampden
  Terrace

Traffic Engineer Jana Robbins reviewed with the Commission the traffic
engineering safety report assessing Westmont Drive onto northbound Main Street
and the speed of traffic as cars curve onto Main Street east towards Hampden
Terrace.

After a thorough review of existing field conditions, speed data and average daily
traffic, it was determined that traffic calming measures be installed along W. Main
Street between Westmont Drive and Hampden Terrace to reduce the speed of
vehicles as they enter W. Main Street.

After discussion, it was moved by Commissioner Chen, seconded by
Commissioner Gutierrez, and carried unanimously, to adopt the recommended
improvements as presented in the report.

2. Traffic Safety Review Poplar Boulevard between Fremont Avenue and the
  City of Alhambra’s West city limit

Traffic Engineer Jana Robbins reviewed the report that was prepared in response
to a citizen request to assess existing conditions along the segment of Poplar
Boulevard between Fremont Avenue and the city of Alhambra’s west city limit.

Page 1 of 3
 The study found that the City has the appropriate traffic calming measures
currently in place for the study segment of Poplar Boulevard between Winchester
Avenue and Fremont Avenue.

Mrs. Lucy Lopez commented that she would like this item postponed as she did
not feel that she was given ample notice to have the residents of Poplar attend the
meeting and provide their statements.

After discussion, it was moved by Commissioner Gutierrez, seconded by
Commissioner Bender, and carried (Commissioner Fortin opposed), to adopt the
recommended improvements as presented in the report with the item to be
agenized at the next Transportation Commission meeting.

3. Traffic Safety Review of Montezuma Avenue between Fremont Avenue
  and Palm Avenue

Traffic Engineer Jana Robbins reviewed the report that was prepared in response
to a citizen request for the installation for a stop sign with stop bar on Date Avenue
at Montezuma Avenue as well as on Primrose Avenue at Montezuma Avenue.

The study recommends the installation of a Stop sign and Stop bar at Primrose
Avenue and Date Avenue as they intersect with Montezuma Avenue. Both of
these locations are along the route to the Granada Park with sidewalks on both
sides of Montezuma Avenue so vehicles exiting along these side streets may
encounter pedestrians.

After discussion, it was moved by Commissioner Gutierrez, seconded by
Commissioner Fortin, and carried unanimously, to adopt the recommended
improvements as presented in the report.

4. Public Comments

Mrs. Lucy Lopez commented that she had items she would email items that she
would like presented to the Transportation Commission.

Meehar Tom commented that there is too much traffic with delivery trucks and
speeding on West Commonwealth.

5. Comments and concerns from Commission Members and/or Staff.

Commissioner Fortin introduced himself to the group and discussed his
background.

6. Adjournment

Page 2 of 3

SUBJECT:  TRAFFIC CALMING ALONG POPLAR BLVD FROM WEST CITY LIMIT TO FREMONT AVE

INTRODUCTION/BACKGROUND

The City of Alhambra initially received a resident request to assess existing conditions along the segment
of Poplar Boulevard between Fremont Avenue and the city of Alhambra’s west city limit. According to the
resident, vehicles are speeding along Poplar Boulevard, as well as ignoring the flashing stop signs posted
on the street. The resident also noted that noise laws are being violated by loud vehicles, as well as five
axle trucks over 15,000 pounds violating their prohibition on this street. The resident stated that there
have been several collisions along the segment due to these violations and is specifically asking for speed
bumps along Poplar Boulevard, adding that Poplar Boulevard is a residential road and has a school where
children frequently travel. As part of the traffic review the following items were reviewed: existing
roadway conditions, 6.25 years of collision history, new daily traffic counts including a 24-hour count by
axle, and output from a 24-hour radar speed sample. This report was first brought before the Traffic
Commission March 10, 2021. At this meeting it was determined that a search of additional collisions from
Alhambra PD records would be undertaken and brought back to the Traffic Commission for review.

EXISTING CONDITIONS

Poplar Boulevard: Per the City’s Master Plan of Streets, Poplar Boulevard is considered a major collector
road with a posted speed limit of 25 mph. Poplar Boulevard runs east/west and is approximately 45-feet
wide with one lane in each direction and a dashed yellow center line with parking allowed on both sides
of the street except during street sweeping hours. The western end of this road segment is at Winchester
Avenue. Land use along this section of Poplar Boulevard is primarily single-family residential.

Poplar Boulevard has several existing traffic calming measures. For instance, White Side Stripes have been
installed along the entire study segment of Poplar Boulevard. There are two existing “Your Speed” Driver
Feedback Radar Speed Signs, one for eastbound travel located on the south side of Poplar Boulevard, just
east of the stop controlled intersection of Poplar Boulevard and Winchester Avenue and one for
westbound travel located on the north side of Poplar Boulevard, approximately 140-feet west of Orange
Grove Avenue. Poplar Boulevard also has existing “25” Pavement legends located adjacent to the existing
25 mph speed limit (R2-1) signs along with six existing Stop sign ahead Warning signs (W3-1), as well as
six “Stop Ahead” pavement legends. There are All-Way Stop controlled intersections along this segment
at the following intersections: Westmont Drive, S Westboro Avenue, Orange Grove Avenue, and S
Meridian Avenue. There are Solar powered Flashing LED Stop (R1-1) Signs located at the intersections of
Westmont Drive, S Westboro Avenue, Orange Grove Avenue, and S Meridian Avenue. During a field visit,
it was observed that the Solar powered Flashing LED Stop (R1-1) Sign for west bound travel along Poplar
Boulevard at Westmont Drive was not flashing and could be in need of service to ensure that it is
functioning properly. There are also “No Trucks over 3 Tons” signs, one for eastbound travel located on
the south side of Poplar Boulevard, approximately 105-feet east of Winchester Avenue, and one for
westbound travel located on the north side of Poplar Boulevard, approximately 35-feet west of Fremont
Avenue.

January 2015 to the most recent available accident data, April 2021. Based on the information provided,
a summary breakdown of the number of collisions per year is shown below. This excludes collisions at

Poplar Boulevard between S. Fremont Street and Winchester Avenue within the study period. An equal

TRAFFIC CALMING DEVICES AND STRATEGIES

Traffic calming is the process of reducing vehicle speeds through the use of both passive devices, such as
signs and striping, and physical devices such as changes in road elevation or path. As part of this study,
traffic speeds, accidents and traffic volumes were used to assess existing conditions along this segment.
The type, design and placement of traffic calming devices depend upon the road classification, desired
traffic speed and types of traffic issues along Poplar Avenue. The following is a list of common traffic
calming measures usually deployed to reduce speeding, increase visibility of signs, decrease running of
Stop signs. As shown in Figure 2 most of the typical traffic calming measures have been installed along
Poplar Avenue. This includes additional signage and pavement legends, beacons on Stop Signs, speed
limit signs and radar speed feedback signs as well as side stripes to visually narrow the travel lanes.

1)  Traffic Education Campaign
2)  Signage and Pavement Legends
3)  Larger Dimension Signs or Beacons on Signs
4)  Traffic Striping

7) Speed Humps: Since there are liability issues with the installation of Speed Humps the City of
  Alhambra has elected to not install speed humps on public streets. Speed humps can be placed in
  private parking lots and in some alleys. A change in this policy would require City Council to adopt a
  resolution to allow the installation of speed humps on public streets.

TRAFFIC CIRCLE

As part of this review the resident asked that the City explore the possibility of installing a Traffic Circle or
Roundabout at the ALL-Way Stop controlled “T” intersection of Poplar Boulevard and Orange Grove
Avenue. A mini roundabout or traffic circle is a circular raised or painted center island where drivers travel
counterclockwise. There are no traffic signals or stop signs in a modern roundabout. Drivers yield at entry
to traffic in the roundabout, then enter the intersection and exit essentially making right turns.

The main advantage of traffic circles is that they reduce the number of conflict points for vehicles.
However, to be effective the traffic circle needs to have a large enough diameter or roadway width for
the circle to be large enough to force vehicles to slow down to make an actual right turn around the circle.
The travel way around the circle would need to provide a travel path that motorists would not run over
the traffic circle and is large enough to provide for gaps in circling traffic to allow for vehicles to enter from
lesser side streets. The design of all traffic circles or mini roundabouts needs to follow CAMUTCD
guidelines. A mini roundabout on a residential street is intended to keep speeds to a minimum. LA County
Guidelines for the Design of Roundabouts requires a roadway width of 60’ feet to accommodate the
splitter islands for approach traffic.

As shown above in Figure 4, if a proposed 20-foot mini-roundabout is installed at the intersection of Poplar
Boulevard and Orange Grove Avenue, there would be a need to remove the 8-foot street parking lanes
along both sides of Poplar Boulevard. Removing street parking would need to be done to accommodate
the installation of splitter islands (at least 6 feet in width) along Poplar Boulevard and along Orange Grove
Avenue. Splitter islands would need to be installed at the mini-roundabout to provide refuge for
pedestrians, to control traffic speed, and to have a place to install traffic signs.

As a result of the existing field conditions along Poplar Boulevard, it is not recommended to install a
roundabout at the All-way Stop controlled intersection of Orange Grove Avenue at Poplar Boulevard.

RECOMMENDATIONS

As a result of extensive field data collection and review of existing traffic conditions it is determined that
the City of Alhambra has the appropriate traffic calming measures currently in place for the study segment
of Poplar Boulevard between Winchester Avenue and Fremont Avenue. The data obtained supports
additional traffic calming measures along this segment. The roadway is not wide enough (60’) to provide
the necessary circle diameter to effectively slow traffic without causing undue delay to emergency
vehicles or impacts to on-street parking for those residents within the splitter island for the approach to
a roundabout. A roundabout is not recommended along Poplar Boulevard. The following measures that
should be undertaken to make the STOP control more visible for approaching motorist are listed below
and shown on Figure 5:
